item.text: The desktop automation path is available through `DISPLAY=:0`, so I can drive the existing Chrome window directly. Next I’m opening `chrome://extensions` and loading `/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension` as an unpacked extension.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "DISPLAY=:0 python3 - <<'PY'
import pyautogui, time, subprocess
pyautogui.PAUSE = 0.25
subprocess.run(['wmctrl','-a','Google Chrome'], env={'DISPLAY':':0'})
time.sleep(0.5)
# Close Chrome update bubble and disk warning if they are present; harmless if clicking page whitespace/buttons.
pyautogui.click(1890, 139)  # close update bubble x
pyautogui.click(1120, 146)  # ignore low disk notification
# Navigate to extensions page
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl','l')
pyautogui.write('chrome://extensions', interval=0.01)
pyautogui.press('enter')
time.sleep(2)
# Enable developer mode (top-right toggle on extensions page)
pyautogui.click(1815, 120)
time.sleep(1)
# Click Load unpacked
pyautogui.click(155, 155)
time.sleep(1)
# In file chooser, type path directly and open
pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl','l')
pyautogui.write('/home/user/Desktop/helloExtension', interval=0.01)
pyautogui.press('enter')
time.sleep(0.6)
pyautogui.press('enter')
time.sleep(2)
print('done')
PY"
